segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making the time, Karen. I wanted to walk through the 38-seat rollout for the support and field ops teams and make sure the June 17 go-live still works on your side.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yep, June 17 is still the date. The only thing I want to confirm is billing. Finance asked whether the invoice can be split, 24 seats to support and 14 to field ops.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, we can split that by cost center on the first invoice. Total annual is $42,180 before tax, and it would show as $26,640 for support and $15,540 for field ops.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. And that includes the onboarding package, right? The two admin trainings and the data import?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct. Two 90-minute admin trainings, import of the last 18 months of records, and the launch checklist session. I have that in the order summary as included services, no separate line item.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. Legal was fine with the 12-month term, but they asked for net 45 instead of net 30 because our payment run is weird in July.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: That’s approved on our side. The order form will show net 45 for the initial invoice and then net 30 on any add-on seats after that.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That works. If we add five more seats in Q4, are they prorated to the same end date?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Exactly. Any seats added before May 31, 2027 prorate to the June 16, 2027 renewal date at the same per-seat rate, $1,110 annually.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Send the order form to me and copy Evan in finance. If it looks like what we discussed, I can sign by Friday.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. You’ll have it this afternoon, and I’ll include the implementation dates in the email: kickoff June 3, import file due June 6, admin training June 11 and June 13.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. That gives us enough time to notify the managers. Thanks, yeah, this is straightforward.
